# ADS: Architecture Description Standard

> A free, open-source standard that prescribes the structure, content, and quality criteria of Solution Architecture Documents (SADs). Built upon ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010, the 4+1 View Model, the cloud Well-Architected Frameworks, and TOGAF. Backed by a formal JSON Schema (Draft 2020-12) for machine validation and generation.

ADS defines which sections a SAD must contain, what each section must answer, and what "good" looks like at three documentation depths (Minimum / Recommended / Comprehensive — mapped to RFC 2119 SHALL / SHOULD / MAY). The current standard version is v1.3.2; the JSON Schema version is v1.0.0. Licensed under CC BY 4.0 (content) and MIT (code).

Three names appear throughout. **ADS** is this standard. **SAD** (Solution Architecture Document) is the document you produce. **HLD** (High Level Design) is the architectural-views and quality-attributes content within a SAD.

## Orientation

- [Overview](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/overview/): Structure, concepts, and rationale of ADS in one page; includes comparison with TOGAF, arc42, and cloud WAFs.
- [Quickstart](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/quickstart/): 30-minute walkthrough to produce a first SAD at Minimum depth.
- [Adopting ADS](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/adoption-guide/): How to roll ADS out in an organisation — evaluate fit, pilot, map to governance, customise, onboard, measure.
- [Conformance and Usage](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/how-to-use/): Conformance levels, depth model, RFC 2119 mapping, terminology, compliance scoring.
- [Depth Cheat Sheet](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/cheat-sheet/): Single-page table of which sections are required at each documentation depth.
- [Design Principles](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/design-principles/): Atomic fields, schema-as-truth, extensibility without ambiguity.
- [Framework Alignment](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/framework-alignment/): Traceability to ISO 42010, 4+1, TOGAF, AWS/Azure WAF.

## The Standard (Sections 0–7)

- [0. Document Control](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/0-document-control/): Metadata, change history, contributors, sign-offs.
- [1. Executive Summary](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/1-executive-summary/): Solution overview, business context and drivers, scope, criticality.
- [2. Stakeholders & Concerns](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/2-stakeholders/): Stakeholder register, concerns matrix, compliance and regulatory context.
- [3. Architectural Views](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/3-views-overview/): How the six architectural views fit together.
- [3.1 Logical View](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/3-1-logical-view/): Components, capabilities, design patterns.
- [3.2 Integration & Data Flow View](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/3-2-integration-view/): How components communicate internally and externally.
- [3.3 Physical View](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/3-3-physical-view/): Hosting, compute, networks, environments.
- [3.4 Data View](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/3-4-data-view/): Data stores, classification, data lifecycle.
- [3.5 Security View](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/3-5-security-view/): Authentication, authorisation, encryption, monitoring, threat model.
- [3.6 Scenarios](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/3-6-scenarios/): Key use cases and Architecture Decision Records (ADRs).
- [4. Architectural Quality Attributes](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/4-quality-attributes-overview/): The five cross-cutting evaluation perspectives.
- [4.1 Operational Excellence](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/4-1-operational-excellence/): Logging, monitoring, alerting, runbooks, operational maturity.
- [4.2 Reliability & Resilience](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/4-2-reliability/): DR strategy, RTO/RPO, backup, fault tolerance.
- [4.3 Performance Efficiency](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/4-3-performance/): Performance targets, growth projections, load testing.
- [4.4 Cost Optimisation](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/4-4-cost-optimisation/): Cost analysis, monitoring, right-sizing.
- [4.5 Sustainability](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/4-5-sustainability/): Carbon-aware hosting, auto-shutdown, sustainability metrics.
- [5. Lifecycle Management](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/5-lifecycle/): CI/CD, migration, test strategy, release, operations, decommissioning, exit planning.
- [6. Decision Making & Governance](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/6-decision-making/): RAID log, technical debt, guardrail exceptions, ADRs, compliance traceability, sign-off.
- [7. Appendices](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/7-appendices/): Glossary, references, supporting standards.

## Schema and Templates

- [JSON Schema (canonical)](https://archstandard.org/schema/v1.0.0/ads.schema.json): machine-readable contract, JSON Schema Draft 2020-12. Validate against this URL.
- [Markdown template](https://archstandard.org/v1/templates/sad-template.md)
- [YAML template](https://archstandard.org/v1/templates/sad-template.yaml)
- [JSON template](https://archstandard.org/v1/templates/sad-template.json)
- [Word template](https://archstandard.org/v1/templates/sad-template.docx)
- [Complete standard PDF](https://archstandard.org/v1/ads-standard-v1.pdf)

## Worked Example SADs

Seven examples, each validated against the schema, covering different industries, scales, and depths.

- [Example: Employee Directory](https://archstandard.org/v1/examples/employee-directory/): Minimum depth — internal HR web app. [JSON](https://archstandard.org/v1/examples/employee-directory.json) [Markdown](https://archstandard.org/v1/examples/employee-directory.md)
- [Example: Customer API Platform](https://archstandard.org/v1/examples/customer-api-platform/): Recommended depth — regulated open-banking API. [JSON](https://archstandard.org/v1/examples/customer-api-platform.json) [Markdown](https://archstandard.org/v1/examples/customer-api-platform.md)
- [Example: Cloud Migration](https://archstandard.org/v1/examples/cloud-migration/): Recommended depth — lift-and-shift to AWS. [JSON](https://archstandard.org/v1/examples/cloud-migration.json) [Markdown](https://archstandard.org/v1/examples/cloud-migration.md)
- [Example: NorthWind Retail Online](https://archstandard.org/v1/examples/northwind-retail/): Recommended depth, Tier 2 — PCI-DSS regulated e-commerce on AWS. [JSON](https://archstandard.org/v1/examples/northwind-retail.json) [Markdown](https://archstandard.org/v1/examples/northwind-retail.md)
- [Example: Medwick Healthcare Trust -- MyMedwick Patient Portal](https://archstandard.org/v1/examples/medwick-healthcare/): Comprehensive depth, Tier 1 — national healthcare patient portal with FHIR R4. [JSON](https://archstandard.org/v1/examples/medwick-healthcare.json) [Markdown](https://archstandard.org/v1/examples/medwick-healthcare.md)
- [Example: Stellar Platform (Internal Developer Platform)](https://archstandard.org/v1/examples/stellar-platform/): Recommended depth, Tier 3 — multi-cloud Internal Developer Platform on Kubernetes. [JSON](https://archstandard.org/v1/examples/stellar-platform.json) [Markdown](https://archstandard.org/v1/examples/stellar-platform.md)
- [Example: archstandard.org](https://archstandard.org/v1/examples/archstandard-org/): Minimum depth — SAD for this very site. [JSON](https://archstandard.org/v1/examples/archstandard-org.json) [Markdown](https://archstandard.org/v1/examples/archstandard-org.md)

## Guidance

- [What Good Looks Like](https://archstandard.org/v1/guidance/what-good-looks-like/): High-quality content excerpts showing what a well-written SAD section looks like.
- [Anti-Patterns](https://archstandard.org/v1/guidance/anti-patterns/): Common mistakes with before-and-after examples.
- [Decision Guides](https://archstandard.org/v1/guidance/decision-guides/): Flowcharts for picking depth, threat modelling, splitting SADs, classifying RAID items.
- [Reviewer Perspectives](https://archstandard.org/v1/guidance/reviewer-perspectives/): What ARB, Security, Data, SRE, Finance, Change, and Product reviewers each look for.
- [Starter Kits](https://archstandard.org/v1/guidance/starter-kits/): Pre-scoped guidance for new cloud apps, migrations, integrations, and platforms.
- [Review Checklist](https://archstandard.org/v1/guidance/review-checklist/): Printable one-pager for governance reviewers.
- [Industry Mappings](https://archstandard.org/v1/guidance/industry-mappings/): Traceability to GDS Service Standard, NIST CSF, PCI-DSS, ISO 27001, NHS DSPT, UK GDPR, FCA.
- [Cheat Cards](https://archstandard.org/v1/guidance/cheat-cards/): One-page printable quick-reference cards.
- [The 2-Minute Pitch](https://archstandard.org/v1/guidance/pitch/): Speaker notes for introducing ADS to an organisation in two minutes.

## Optional

- [Templates](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/templates/): How to use templates, customise per organisation, and convert between formats.
- [Downloads](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/downloads/): All downloadable files in one place.
- [AI Prompts Library](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/prompts/): AI prompt library — first-draft, validation, scoring, improvement, security and governance review.
- [JSON Schema](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/schema/): JSON Schema structure, validation instructions in Node and Python.
- [Frequently Asked Questions](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/faq/): Frequently asked questions about ADS.
- [Version History](https://archstandard.org/v1/standard/version-history/): Release notes and schema-compatibility table.
- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/andibing/archstandard): source for the site, schema, templates, and examples.
- [Full content (llms-full.txt)](https://archstandard.org/llms-full.txt): all page content concatenated for LLM ingestion.
